assessment.bestSupportedCause: The browser check began while an edge still served the previous Worker version. That version returned 404 for a JavaScript asset needed by the page; the check then failed about 30 seconds later. A missing script preventing hydration is the strongest explanation.
assessment.confidence: high for a mixed-version asset failure; the precise Playwright assertion is unproved because the original exception was deliberately sanitised
assessment.expectedMissingRoute404: The 404 for /__docs-evidence__/missing is an expected test assertion, unlike the JavaScript asset 404.
assessment.readbackLimit: The Cloudflare deployment API reported the new version at 100% traffic, but that control-plane readback did not prove every edge had stopped serving the previous version.

recovery.operation: The hosted browser check now retries only when a hashed JavaScript asset returns 404 during failed hydration. A separate credential-free GitHub check passed against the already deployed Production Worker.

nonClaims: Cloudflare invocation logs do not contain the browser's raw Playwright exception or prove the exact line that timed out.
The original GitHub deployment run remains failed and cannot be retroactively changed to success.
No Production apply, rollback, DNS change, custom-domain change or publication was performed during this investigation or recovery.
A Production rollback was not exercised because the live Worker passed the separate hosted check without one.
